title: Youth Welfare Support Act
full_text:
YOUTH WELFARE SUPPORT ACT

CHAPTER 1 GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 (Purpose)
This Act sets out matters concerning the improvement of youth welfare pursuant to Article 49(4) of the Framework Act on Youth.

Article 2 (Definitions)
Terms used in this Act are defined as follows: <Amended 2021.3.23; 2025.12.30>
1. "Youth" means a person falling under the main clause of Article 3, subparagraph 1 of the Framework Act on Youth.
2. "Youth welfare" means youth welfare under Article 3, subparagraph 4 of the Framework Act on Youth.
3. "Guardian" means a person with parental authority, a legal representative, or a person actually raising a youth.
4. "Youth in crisis" means a youth lacking conditions necessary for harmonious and healthy growth and life, including one experiencing family problems or difficulty with academic performance or social adaptation.
5. "Out-of-home youth" means a youth in crisis separated from a guardian due to domestic conflict, abuse, violence, neglect, family dissolution, running away, or similar reasons and needing social protection and support.
5-2. "Isolated or reclusive youth" means a youth in crisis whose daily life is substantially impaired because the youth has almost no interaction with others or lives only in a limited residential space for a considerable period or longer.
6. "Youth parents" means persons raising a child where both parents are youth.

Article 2-2 (Surveys of Actual Conditions)
(1) The Minister of Gender Equality and Family shall conduct a survey of youth in crisis every 3 years and publish its results, to identify the causes and circumstances of their crises and provide basic data needed to formulate policies to improve youth welfare. <Amended 2022.12.27; 2025.10.1>
(2) If necessary for the survey under paragraph (1), the Minister of Gender Equality and Family may request the heads of relevant central administrative agencies, local governments, public institutions under the Act on the Management of Public Institutions, and other relevant corporations or organizations to submit necessary data or state their opinions. A person receiving such a request shall cooperate unless there is a justifiable reason not to do so. <Amended 2025.10.1>
(3) Matters necessary for the subjects, methods and procedures of the survey under paragraph (1), publication of its results, and related matters shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Gender Equality and Family. <Amended 2025.10.1>

CHAPTER 2 PREFERENTIAL TREATMENT FOR YOUTH

Article 3 (Preferential Treatment for Youth)
(1) The State or a local government may waive or reduce charges when youth use transportation, cultural, leisure, or other facilities it operates.
(2) Where any of the following persons operates a facility used by youth, the State or a local government may recommend that the person reduce its charges for youth:
1. A person receiving financial subsidies from the State or a local government;
2. A person receiving tax benefits under relevant legislation;
3. A person performing work entrusted by the State or a local government.
(3) A youth seeking a waiver or reduction under paragraph (1) or (2) shall present the facility manager with proof or material verifying age, such as a resident registration card (including a mobile resident registration card), student identification card, or youth card under Article 4. <Amended 2023.12.26>
(4) The types of facilities eligible for waivers or reductions under paragraph (1) or (2), the age criteria for youth, and related matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 4 (Youth Cards)
(1) A Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Special Self-Governing Province Governor, or head of a Si, Gun, or Gu (a Gu means an autonomous Gu; hereinafter the same applies) may issue youth cards to youth aged 9 through 18. <Amended 2018.12.18>
(2) A youth card under paragraph (1) shall not be transferred or lent to another person.
(3) No person shall manufacture or use a certificate bearing the same name or marking as a youth card other than the youth card under paragraph (1).
(4) Matters necessary for issuing youth cards under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Gender Equality and Family. <Amended 2025.10.1>

CHAPTER 3 YOUTH HEALTH PROTECTION

Article 5 (Support for Healthy Growth)
(1) The State and local governments shall formulate necessary measures, including disease prevention and health education, to promote youth health and improve physical fitness, taking sex-specific characteristics into account. Guardians shall endeavor to promote the health and improve the physical fitness of the youth they raise. <Amended 2016.12.20>
(2) In consultation with relevant institutions, the State and local governments may establish and disseminate health and physical fitness standards for youth reflecting sex-specific characteristics. <Amended 2016.12.20>
(3) To support the healthy growth of female youth, the State and local governments shall provide menstrual products when female youth apply for them. <Added 2017.12.12; amended 2021.4.20>
(4) Matters necessary for preparing the measures under paragraph (1), establishing and disseminating the standards under paragraph (2), and the criteria, scope, methods, application and payment procedures for menstrual product support under paragraph (3), and related matters, shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended 2017.12.12; 2021.4.20>

Article 6 (Physical Fitness Tests and Health Examinations)
(1) The State and local governments may conduct physical fitness tests and health examinations for youth.
(2) The State and local governments shall inform the youth themselves of the results of the tests and examinations under paragraph (1).
(3) The State and local governments may entrust specialized institutions or organizations with conducting the tests and examinations and notifying the results under paragraphs (1) and (2).
(4) Matters necessary for conducting the tests and examinations and notifying the results under paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Gender Equality and Family. <Amended 2025.10.1>

Article 7 (Analysis of Health Examination Results)
(1) The State and local governments shall analyze the results of health examinations under Article 6 and formulate and implement measures necessary to promote youth health.
(2) The State and local governments may commission specialized institutions to perform the analysis under paragraph (1).

Article 8 (Prohibition on Disclosure of Health Examination Results)
A person currently or formerly working for the State, a local government, or a specialized institution or organization that conducted health examinations under Article 6 shall not disclose their results, except where disclosure is unavoidable to formulate or implement the measures under Article 7(1).

CHAPTER 4 COMMUNITY INTEGRATED YOUTH SUPPORT SYSTEMS

Article 9 (Establishment and Operation of Community Integrated Youth Support Systems)
(1) The head of a local government shall establish and operate a community integrated youth support system (hereinafter an "integrated support system") through which local governments, public institutions, youth organizations under Article 3, subparagraph 8 of the Framework Act on Youth, and others cooperate in performing their work, to identify and protect youth in crisis within the jurisdiction at an early stage and efficiently carry out youth welfare and youth protection under Article 3, subparagraph 5 of that Act.
(2) The State shall support the establishment and operation of integrated support systems.
(3) Matters necessary for the composition of integrated support systems, including the institutions or organizations that must be included, shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 9-2 (Dedicated Bodies for Integrated Support Systems)
(1) A Special Metropolitan City, Metropolitan City, Special Self-Governing City, Do, Special Self-Governing Province, or Si, Gun, or Gu (a Gu means an autonomous Gu; hereinafter the same applies) may establish a body dedicated to the integrated support system to efficiently carry out its work.
(2) Dedicated public officials and private-sector specialists may be assigned to the body under paragraph (1), as prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Gender Equality and Family. <Amended 2025.10.1>
(3) Relevant administrative agencies, youth organizations under Article 3, subparagraph 8 of the Framework Act on Youth (hereinafter "youth organizations"), and persons establishing and operating youth facilities under Article 3, subparagraph 6 of that Act shall cooperate with the dedicated public officials and private-sector specialists in performing their duties.
(4) Matters necessary for the scope of duties, organization and operation of the body under paragraph (1), appointment of dedicated public officials under paragraph (2), and related matters shall be prescribed by ordinance of the relevant local government.

Article 10 (Youth Welfare Deliberation Committees)
(1) If considered necessary for smooth operation of an integrated support system, the head of a local government may establish a youth welfare deliberation committee (hereinafter a "deliberation committee") to deliberate on matters prescribed by Presidential Decree, including policies concerning the welfare and protection of youth in crisis. <Amended 2021.3.23>
(2) A deliberation committee shall consist of heads or staff of the institutions and organizations making up the integrated support system and other persons with extensive knowledge and experience in youth welfare. <Amended 2021.3.23>
(3) A deliberation committee may establish a working committee if considered necessary for efficient deliberation. <Added 2021.3.23>
(4) Beyond paragraphs (1) through (3), matters necessary for operating deliberation and working committees, including composition, appointment of members and meeting procedures, shall be prescribed by rules of the relevant local government. <Amended 2021.3.23>

Article 11 (Support for Residents' Voluntary Activities)
Where local residents voluntarily form an organization and engage in activities to identify, protect and support youth in crisis, the State and local governments may support that organization's activities.

Article 12 (Counseling and Installation of Telephone Services)
(1) The State and local governments shall enable all youth to receive expert counseling on matters they need.
(2) The State and local governments shall install and operate telephone services or operate information and communications networks for the counseling under paragraph (1).
(3) Matters necessary for installing and operating the telephone services and operating the information and communications networks under paragraph (2) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 12-2 (Establishment and Operation of the Integrated Information System for Supporting Youth in Crisis)
(1) To operate integrated support systems efficiently through effective processing and sharing of information on youth in crisis and coordination of services among institutions, the Minister of Gender Equality and Family may establish and operate an integrated information system for supporting youth in crisis (hereinafter the "integrated information system"), as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended 2025.10.1>
(2) With the explicit consent of the data subject, the Minister of Gender Equality and Family may collect, retain, use, provide and link any of the following information needed to establish and operate the integrated information system: <Amended 2021.12.7; 2025.10.1>
1. Information on operation of community integrated youth support systems under Article 9;
2. Information on expert counseling under Article 12;
3. Information on counseling and education for families and guardians of youth in crisis under Article 13;
4. Information on special support for youth in crisis under Article 14;
5. Information on support for out-of-home youth under Article 16;
6. Information on support for youth with a migrant background under Article 18;
7. Information on preventive and restorative protective support under Article 19;
8. Information on youth counseling and welfare centers under Article 29;
9. Information on youth welfare facilities under Article 31;
10. Information concerning support centers for out-of-school youth under Article 12 of the Act on Support for Out-of-School Youth;
11. Information concerning prevention of addiction to and excessive immersion in Internet games, and support for affected youth, under Article 27 of the Youth Protection Act;
12. Information concerning youth protection and rehabilitation centers under Article 35 of the Youth Protection Act;
13. Youth-related information among social security benefits under Article 2, subparagraph 1 of the Act on the Use and Provision of Social Security Benefits and Search for Eligible Beneficiaries;
14. Resident registration data or information under the Resident Registration Act;
15. Family relations registration data or information under the Act on Registration of Family Relations;
16. Other information needed to perform work supporting youth in crisis as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(3) The Minister of Gender Equality and Family may request relevant central administrative agencies, local governments and related institutions and organizations (hereinafter "relevant central administrative agencies and others") to provide data and information needed to establish and operate the integrated information system, and may collect, retain and use them within the purposes for which they were provided. Those receiving such a request shall comply unless there is a justifiable reason not to do so. <Amended 2025.10.1>
(4) To protect and support youth in crisis effectively, the Minister of Gender Equality and Family may take measures to link necessary information with private organizations and institutions processing the information listed in paragraph (2). Those organizations and institutions may use the linked information within the purposes of the linkage. <Amended 2025.10.1>
(5) Relevant central administrative agencies and others shall consult the Minister of Gender Equality and Family in advance if they need to use data or information held by the integrated information system. The Minister may provide information to them to the extent needed for their relevant work, and recipients may retain and use it only for the purposes for which it was provided. <Amended 2025.10.1>
(6) The Minister of Gender Equality and Family shall prepare measures necessary to protect personal information throughout establishment and operation of the integrated information system. <Amended 2025.10.1>
(7) For the work under paragraph (1), the integrated information system may operate through connections to relevant computer networks, including the social security information system under Article 37(2) of the Framework Act on Social Security.
(8) The Minister of Gender Equality and Family may entrust operation of the integrated information system to the Korea Youth Counseling and Welfare Institute under Article 22. <Amended 2025.10.1>
(9) A person acquiring, managing or using data or information in the integrated information system under paragraphs (2) through (5) shall not use data or information learned through those duties for other purposes or provide or disclose them to a third party.
(10) Other matters necessary for establishment and operation of the integrated support system shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

CHAPTER 5 SUPPORT FOR YOUTH IN CRISIS

Article 13 (Counseling and Education)
(1) The State and local governments may provide counseling and education to the families and guardians of youth in crisis to ensure efficient and appropriate support for those youth.
(2) When the State or a local government recommends counseling and education, the families and guardians of youth in crisis shall cooperate and participate conscientiously.
(3) Where families or guardians with income at or below the level prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Gender Equality and Family receive counseling and education under paragraph (1), the State and local governments may reimburse actual expenses, including travel expenses, within budgetary limits. <Amended 2025.10.1>

Article 14 (Special Support for Youth in Crisis)
(1) The State and local governments may provide necessary social and economic support to youth in crisis (hereinafter "special support"), as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(2) Special support shall be provided in the form of goods or services according to the particulars prescribed by Presidential Decree, including support for living expenses, schooling, medical care, vocational training and youth activities. However, monetary support may be provided if considered indispensable to supporting youth in crisis.
(3) Selection criteria, scope and duration for youth receiving special support, and other necessary matters, shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 15 (Applications for and Selection for Special Support)
(1) Any of the following persons may apply to the Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Special Self-Governing Province Governor, or head of a Si, Gun, or Gu to select a youth in crisis for special support. A guardian under subparagraph 1 or a person under subparagraphs 2 through 5 shall obtain the consent of the youth concerned: <Amended 2018.12.18>
1. The youth or the youth's guardian;
2. A youth leader under Article 3, subparagraph 7 of the Framework Act on Youth;
3. A teacher under Article 19(1) of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act;
4. A social worker under Article 11 of the Social Welfare Services Act;
5. A public official responsible for youth affairs in a local government.
(2) Upon receiving an application under paragraph (1), the Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Special Self-Governing Province Governor, or head of a Si, Gun, or Gu shall decide whether to select the youth and determine the details and duration of support following deliberation by the deliberation committee. <Amended 2018.12.18; 2021.3.23>
(3) If urgent support is considered necessary or no deliberation committee has been formed, the Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Special Self-Governing Province Governor, or head of a Si, Gun, or Gu may make the decision under paragraph (2) without committee deliberation. <Amended 2018.12.18; 2021.3.23>

Article 16 (Support for Out-of-Home Youth)
(1) The Minister of Gender Equality and Family or head of a local government shall formulate and implement policies, including education, public information, research and surveys, to prevent youth from becoming out-of-home youth and to support such youth. <Amended 2021.3.23; 2023.10.24; 2025.10.1>
(2) The State and local governments shall take necessary measures, including counseling, protection, support for self-reliance and follow-up care, to help out-of-home youth return to their families and society. <Added 2021.3.23>
(3) Guardians shall endeavor to prevent youth from becoming out-of-home youth and actively cooperate with efforts by the State, local governments and others to enable out-of-home youth to return to their families and society. <Amended 2021.3.23>
(4) The Minister of Gender Equality and Family or head of a local government may entrust youth organizations with the prevention, protection and support work under paragraphs (1) and (2). <Amended 2021.3.23; 2025.10.1>

Article 16-2 (Support for Isolated or Reclusive Youth)
(1) The State and local governments may provide counseling, education, relationship-building programs, and other support to help isolated or reclusive youth adapt to society and pursue their studies.
(2) The Minister of Gender Equality and Family or head of a local government may entrust the duties under paragraph (1) to any of the following institutions or organizations:
1. Youth counseling and welfare centers under Article 29;
2. Out-of-school youth support centers under Article 12 of the Act on Support for Out-of-School Youth;
3. Youth organizations under Article 3, subparagraph 8 of the Framework Act on Youth;
4. Other institutions or organizations recognized by the Minister as having the specialized personnel and facilities needed to support isolated or reclusive youth.

Article 16-3 (Support for Return and Adaptation to School)
The State and local governments (including superintendents of education) shall provide necessary support so that youth in crisis can return or adapt to school smoothly.

Article 17 Deleted. <2014.5.28>

Article 18 (Support for Youth with a Migrant Background)
The State and local governments shall prepare and implement necessary measures, including counseling and education, to help youth in either of the following categories adapt to society and improve their learning abilities:
1. Youth in multicultural families under Article 2, subparagraph 1 of the Multicultural Families Support Act;
2. Other youth who have migrated to Korea and experience difficulties in social adaptation or schooling.

CHAPTER 5-2 SUPPORT FOR YOUTH PARENTS <Added 2021.3.23>

Article 18-2 (Family Support Services for Youth Parents)
(1) The State and local governments may provide youth parents with the following family support services:
1. Childrearing and education services;
2. Home-visit health management services under Article 11(1)5(g) of the Regional Public Health Act;
3. Services to improve family relationships, including education and counseling;
4. Other family support services for youth parents prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(2) Selection criteria, scope and duration for youth parents receiving family support services under paragraph (1), and other necessary matters, shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 18-3 (Welfare Support for Youth Parents)
(1) The State and local governments may provide welfare support to youth parents and their children.
(2) Support under paragraph (1) shall be provided in money, goods, or services, including child-rearing cost support, livelihood support, medical support, housing support, and youth activity support, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended 2025.12.30>
(3) Selection criteria, scope, duration, and other necessary matters for youth parents eligible under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. Eligibility and the amount or content of support may differ according to income and assets, employment status, and whether the same support is received under other statutes prescribed by Presidential Decree, including the National Basic Living Security Act. <Amended 2025.12.30>

Article 18-4 (Provision of Financial Information)
(1) Where investigation of financial information is necessary to verify whether youth parents applying for welfare support under Article 18-3(1) (hereinafter "welfare support") meet the selection criteria under paragraph (3) of that Article (hereinafter in this Article "welfare support criteria"), the head of the central administrative agency or local government providing support shall obtain written consent (including an electronic document under Article 2, subparagraph 1 of the Framework Act on Electronic Documents and Transactions) to provision of the following data or information (hereinafter "financial information, etc."):
1. Financial information: Average deposit balances and other data or information prescribed by Presidential Decree among data or information concerning financial assets and transactions under Article 2, subparagraphs 2 and 3 of the Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality;
2. Credit information: Debts and other data or information prescribed by Presidential Decree among credit information under Article 2, subparagraph 1 of the Credit Information Use and Protection Act;
3. Insurance information: Premiums paid for insurance under Article 4(1) of the Insurance Business Act and other data or information prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(2) Notwithstanding Article 4(1) of the Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality and Article 32(1) of the Credit Information Use and Protection Act, the Minister of Gender Equality and Family may request financial information, etc. from the heads of financial institutions, etc. (financial companies, etc. under Article 2, subparagraph 1 of the former Act and credit information concentration institutions under Article 2, subparagraph 6 of the latter Act; hereinafter "financial institutions, etc.") using a document electronically converted from the written consent submitted under paragraph (1).
(3) Where necessary to investigate whether youth parents receiving support continue to meet welfare support criteria, the Minister may, notwithstanding Article 4(1) of the Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality and Article 32(1) of the Credit Information Use and Protection Act, request their financial information, etc. from the heads of financial institutions, etc. by a document containing personal particulars or through an information network, according to standards prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(4) Heads of financial institutions, etc. receiving a request under paragraph (2) or (3) shall provide the account holder's financial information, etc., notwithstanding Article 4 of the Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality and Article 32 of the Credit Information Use and Protection Act.
(5) The head providing the information shall notify the account holder. If the account holder consents, notification may be omitted notwithstanding Article 4-2(1) of the Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality and Articles 32(7) and 35(2) of the Credit Information Use and Protection Act.
(6) Requests and provision shall use an information network under Article 2(1)1 of the Act on Promotion of Information and Communications Network Utilization and Information Protection, except for unavoidable reasons such as damage to the network.
(7) Methods, procedures, standards, and other necessary matters for requesting and providing financial information, etc. shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 18-5 (Educational support to youth parents) (1) The State and local governments may provide any of the following support at the choice of youth parents to enable them to continue their study: <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  1. Support for remaining enrolled in the register of a school defined in Article 2 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act and support for educational expenses or a school graduation equivalency examination;
  2. Support for educational expenses to academic ability-accredited lifelong educational establishments under Article 31(2) of the Lifelong Education Act;
  3. Educational support under Article 28 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act;
  4. Other matters prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Gender Equality and Family for providing educational support to youth parents.
  (2) In order for youth parents to go to school and rear children at the same time, the State and local governments may support to enable the children to use the workplace child care centers established in the schools prescribed in Article 2 of the Higher Education Act to which the youth parents belong.
  (3) The Minister of Gender Equality and Family shall request cooperation from the Minister of Education so that young parents can continue their study. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  (4) Criteria for selection of youth parents entitled to educational support prescribed in paragraphs (1) and (2), scope and period thereof, and other necessary matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [This Article Added  on Mar. 23, 2021]

Article 18-6 (Providing youth parents with vocational experience and support for employment) (1) The State and local governments may provide the following support for youth parents to enable them to gain vocational experience and to receive training so that they can build a stable childrearing environment:
  1. Vocational aptitude tests and vocational guidance counseling programs;
  2. Vocational experience and training programs;
  3. Introduction and management of careers;
  4. Other matters necessary for youth parents to gain vocational experience and to receive training.
  (2) The State and local governments may conduct vocational education and training for youth parents in order to enable them to acquire and improve knowledge, skills, and attitudes necessary for finding employment and performing their duties.
  [This Article Added  on Mar. 23, 2021]

CHAPTER 6 PREVENTIVE AND RESTORATIVE PROTECTIVE SUPPORT <Amended 2018.12.18>

Article 19 (Provision of Preventive and Restorative Protective Support)
(1) To prevent youth delinquency and deviant behavior and help youth return and adapt to family, school and social life, a Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Special Self-Governing Province Governor, or head of a Si, Gun, or Gu may provide preventive and restorative protective support (hereinafter "protective support") to a youth in either of the following categories upon application by the youth, the youth's guardian, or the principal of the school the youth attends. If the guardian or principal applies, the youth's consent shall be obtained. <Amended 2018.12.18>
1. A youth who has engaged in delinquent or deviant behavior;
2. A youth who has difficulty adapting to everyday life and needs educational help outside the home or school.
(2) Protective support shall follow methods prescribed by Presidential Decree, including counseling, education, volunteering, training, sports and group activities, that assist the youth in returning and adapting to normal family, school and social life. <Amended 2018.12.18>
(3) Protective support shall last no longer than 6 months. However, after reviewing its results, a Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Special Self-Governing Province Governor, or head of a Si, Gun, or Gu who considers an extension necessary may extend it once for up to 6 months with the youth's consent. <Amended 2018.12.18>
(4) Selection criteria and procedures for recipients of protective support shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Gender Equality and Family. <Amended 2018.12.18; 2025.10.1>

Article 20 (Establishment and Operation of Facilities)
The State and local governments shall endeavor to ensure that protective support is effective, including by establishing and operating necessary facilities, developing and disseminating protective support programs, supporting protective support activities, and educating leaders. <Amended 2018.12.18>

Article 21 (Protective Support Guardians)
(1) The State and local governments (where protective support work is entrusted under Article 42(2), the youth organization entrusted with that work) may designate protective support guardians to guide individual youth receiving protective support on a dedicated basis. <Amended 2018.12.18>
(2) Protective support guardians under paragraph (1) shall be designated from among youth leaders under Article 3, subparagraph 7 of the Framework Act on Youth and youth guidance committee members under Article 27 of that Act. <Amended 2018.12.18>
(3) Details of the duties and designation criteria for protective support guardians under paragraph (1), and related matters, shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Gender Equality and Family. <Amended 2018.12.18; 2025.10.1>

CHAPTER 7 YOUTH WELFARE SUPPORT INSTITUTIONS

Article 22 (Korea Youth Counseling and Welfare Institute)
(1) The State shall establish the Korea Youth Counseling and Welfare Institute (hereinafter the "Youth Counseling Institute") to support formulation of youth welfare policies and implement programs efficiently and systematically. <Amended 2021.3.23>

(2) The Youth Counseling Institute shall perform the following duties: <Added 2021.3.23>
1. Research on policies concerning youth counseling and welfare;
2. Development, operation and support of youth counseling and welfare programs;
3. Development of youth counseling techniques and production and dissemination of counseling materials;
4. Training and education of youth counseling and welfare personnel;
5. Coordination among and support for institutions concerned with youth counseling and welfare;
6. Guidance and support for youth counseling and welfare centers, youth welfare facilities, and support centers for out-of-school youth under Article 12 of the Act on Support for Out-of-School Youth;
7. Counseling and education for families of youth;
8. Operation of the integrated information system;
9. Maintenance, management and operation of youth treatment and rehabilitation centers established by the State and youth protection and rehabilitation centers under Article 35(1) of the Youth Protection Act;
10. Other incidental activities necessary to fulfill the purposes of the Youth Counseling Institute.
(3) The Youth Counseling Institute shall be a corporation. <Amended 2021.3.23>
(4) The Youth Counseling Institute may establish branch institutes as provided in its articles of incorporation. <Amended 2021.3.23>
(5) The Youth Counseling Institute shall come into existence upon registration of its establishment at the location of its principal office. <Amended 2021.3.23>

Article 23 (Articles of Incorporation)
(1) The Youth Counseling Institute's articles of incorporation shall include the following:
1. Purpose;
2. Name;
3. Location of its principal office;
4. Matters concerning its activities;
5. Matters concerning executives and employees;
6. Matters concerning the board of directors;
7. Matters concerning assets and accounting;
8. Matters concerning duties and their execution;
9. Matters concerning amendments to the articles of incorporation.
(2) The Youth Counseling Institute shall obtain authorization from the Minister of Gender Equality and Family to amend its articles of incorporation. <Amended 2025.10.1>

Article 24 (Submission of Business Plans)
(1) The Youth Counseling Institute shall prepare a business plan and budget as prescribed by Presidential Decree and submit them to the Minister of Gender Equality and Family for approval before the business year begins. <Amended 2025.10.1>
(2) Upon the end of a fiscal year, the Youth Counseling Institute shall promptly prepare its statement of accounts for that year, select a certified public accountant or accounting corporation as prescribed by rules of the Board of Audit and Inspection and undergo an accounting audit, submit the audited statement to the Minister of Gender Equality and Family by the end of February of the following fiscal year, and obtain approval by the end of March to finalize the accounts. <Amended 2015.2.3; 2025.10.1>

Article 25 (Subsidies and Contributions)
(1) Within budgetary limits, the Government may contribute or subsidize all or part of the expenses needed for the Youth Counseling Institute's activities and operation. <Amended 2014.3.24>
(2) An individual, corporation or organization may contribute or donate money or other property to support the operation or activities of the Youth Counseling Institute.

Article 26 (Executives)
(1) The Youth Counseling Institute shall have no more than 15 directors, including 1 chairperson, and 1 auditor. <Amended 2016.12.20>
(2) Directors other than the chairperson (hereinafter in this Article, "directors") and the auditor shall serve on a non-standing basis. <Amended 2016.12.20>
(3) The Minister of Gender Equality and Family shall appoint and dismiss directors, whose terms of office shall be 2 years. <Amended 2025.10.1>
(4) The Minister of Finance and Economy shall appoint and dismiss the auditor from among multiple candidates recommended by the Executive Recommendation Committee under Article 29 of the Act on the Management of Public Institutions (hereinafter the "Executive Recommendation Committee"). The auditor's term of office shall be 2 years. <Amended 2025.10.1>

Article 27 (Chairperson)
(1) The Minister of Gender Equality and Family shall appoint and dismiss the chairperson from among multiple candidates recommended by the Executive Recommendation Committee. The chairperson's term of office shall be 3 years. <Amended 2016.12.20; 2025.10.1>
(2) The chairperson shall represent the Youth Counseling Institute and oversee its affairs. <Amended 2016.12.20>

Article 28 (Application of the Civil Act)
Except as provided in this Act and the Act on the Management of Public Institutions, the provisions of the Civil Act concerning incorporated foundations shall apply mutatis mutandis to the Youth Counseling Institute.

Article 29 (Youth Counseling and Welfare Centers)
(1) A Special Metropolitan City Mayor, Metropolitan City Mayor, Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Do Governor, or Special Self-Governing Province Governor (hereinafter a "Mayor or Do Governor"), or head of a Si, Gun, or Gu may establish and operate a youth counseling and welfare center to perform work including youth counseling, emergency rescue, rehabilitation toward self-reliance, and medical support. <Amended 2018.12.18>
(2) Youth counseling and welfare centers established under paragraph (1) in Special Metropolitan Cities, Metropolitan Cities, Special Self-Governing Cities, Dos and Special Self-Governing Provinces shall guide and support the work of centers in Sis, Guns and Gus. <Amended 2018.12.18>
(3) A head of a Si, Gun, or Gu may operate the youth counseling and welfare center established under paragraph (1) jointly with the local youth activity promotion center established in that Si, Gun, or Gu under Article 7(1) of the Youth Activity Promotion Act. <Amended 2014.1.21>
(4) A Mayor or Do Governor or head of a Si, Gun, or Gu may entrust a youth organization with operating a youth counseling and welfare center.
(5) A Mayor or Do Governor or head of a Si, Gun, or Gu may establish a youth counseling and welfare center as a corporation.
(6) Specific details of the work under paragraph (1), standards for establishing and operating youth counseling and welfare centers, staff qualifications, and other necessary matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 30 (Support Centers for Youth with a Migrant Background)
(1) The Minister of Gender Equality and Family may establish and operate support centers for youth with a migrant background to provide the support under Article 18. <Amended 2025.10.1>
(2) Matters necessary for establishing and operating support centers for youth with a migrant background shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

CHAPTER 8 YOUTH WELFARE FACILITIES

Article 31 (Types of Youth Welfare Facilities)
The types of youth welfare facilities under Article 17 of the Framework Act on Youth (hereinafter "youth welfare facilities") shall be as follows: <Amended 2016.5.29; 2021.3.23>
1. Youth shelter: A facility that protects out-of-home youth for a specified period and provides counseling and support for housing, schooling and self-reliance to enable them to return to and live in their families, schools and society;
2. Youth self-reliance support center: A facility that helps youth develop the abilities and conditions to live independently where, despite receiving support from a youth shelter or youth recovery support facility for a specified period, they cannot return to and live in their families, schools and society;
3. Youth treatment and rehabilitation center: A residential facility providing comprehensive treatment, education and rehabilitation suited to youth with learning, emotional or behavioral difficulties to enable normal growth and life;
4. Youth recovery support facility: A facility providing counseling, housing, schooling, self-reliance and other services through persons able to protect youth in place of their guardians, for youth subject to an order entrusting their care under Article 32(1)1 of the Juvenile Act.

Article 32 (Establishment of Youth Welfare Facilities)
(1) The State or a local government shall establish and operate youth welfare facilities pursuant to Article 18(1) of the Framework Act on Youth.
(2) A person other than the State or a local government intending to establish and operate a youth welfare facility shall file a report with the Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Special Self-Governing Province Governor, or head of a Si, Gun, or Gu having jurisdiction over the facility's location. <Amended 2018.12.18>
(3) Within the period prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Gender Equality and Family from receipt of a report under paragraph (2), the Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Special Self-Governing Province Governor, or head of a Si, Gun, or Gu shall notify the reporting person whether the report has been accepted. <Added 2018.12.18; amended 2025.10.1>
(4) If, within the period specified in paragraph (3), the Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Special Self-Governing Province Governor, or head of a Si, Gun, or Gu does not notify the reporting person of acceptance or non-acceptance, or of an extension of the processing period under legislation concerning civil petition processing, the report shall be deemed accepted on the day following expiry of that period (where the processing period is extended or re-extended under that legislation, the relevant extended processing period). <Added 2018.12.18>
(5) A person establishing and operating a youth welfare facility shall obtain insurance to compensate for harm to the life or body of youth using the facility, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended 2018.12.18>
(6) Matters necessary for establishing and operating youth welfare facilities under paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree; matters necessary for the methods and procedures for reports under paragraph (2) shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Gender Equality and Family. <Amended 2018.12.18; 2025.10.1>

Article 32-2 (Use of Youth Shelters by Out-of-Home Youth)
(1) When a minor out-of-home youth is admitted to a youth shelter, its operator shall notify the youth's guardian of admission. <Added 2025.12.30>
(2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), notification may be omitted in either of the following cases; in the case of subparagraph 1, notification to the guardian is prohibited. <Added 2025.12.30>
1. Admission due to domestic violence, sexual violence by relatives, or child abuse;
2. Unavoidable cases prescribed by Presidential Decree, including inability to determine the guardian's contact details.
(3) An operator of a youth shelter (excluding a shelter temporarily protecting out-of-home youth for up to seven days; hereinafter the same applies in this Article) shall not discharge an admitted out-of-home youth against the youth's will where admission was due to the reasons in paragraph (2)1, except where the youth:
1. Entered the shelter by false or improper means;
2. Engaged in seriously disorderly conduct in the shelter.
<Amended 2021.3.23; 2021.4.20; 2025.12.30>
(4) When discharging a youth under the proviso of paragraph (3), the operator shall endeavor to take necessary protective measures, including admission to another youth welfare facility, as prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Gender Equality and Family. <Added/amended 2021.4.20; 2025.10.1; 2025.12.30>

Article 32-3 (Support for Self-Reliance)
(1) The State and local governments may take the following measures to enable out-of-home youth to become self-reliant after leaving youth welfare facilities:
1. Support for housing, living expenses, education, employment and other needs for self-reliance;
2. Payment of settlement grants and allowances for self-reliance;
3. Support for building and managing assets needed for self-reliance;
4. Establishment and operation of a follow-up care system;
5. Other matters prescribed by Presidential Decree as necessary for support for self-reliance.
(2) Procedures and methods for support under paragraph (1), the scope of out-of-home youth needing that support, and other necessary matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 33 (Reports of Suspension or Closure)
A person other than the State or a local government intending to suspend, close or resume operation of a youth welfare facility reported under Article 32(2) shall report this in advance to the competent Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Special Self-Governing Province Governor, or head of a Si, Gun, or Gu, as prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Gender Equality and Family. Upon receiving a suspension or closure report, that official shall review its contents and accept it if it complies with this Act. <Amended 2018.12.18; 2025.10.1>

Article 34 (Staff of Youth Welfare Facilities)
(1) Each youth welfare facility shall have the staff necessary to carry out its activities and operation.
(2) The Minister of Gender Equality and Family or head of a local government shall provide education and training to develop youth welfare facility staff and improve their expertise. <Amended 2025.10.1>
(3) The State and local governments shall prepare safety measures to protect the personal safety of youth welfare facility staff. <Added 2023.10.24>
(4) Staff qualification and staffing standards and matters necessary for education and training under paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Gender Equality and Family. <Amended 2023.10.24; 2025.10.1>

Article 35 (Facility Improvement, Suspension of Activities and Closure)
(1) Where a youth welfare facility reported by a person other than the State or a local government falls into any of the following categories, the Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Special Self-Governing Province Governor, or head of a Si, Gun, or Gu may order facility improvements, suspension of activities for no longer than 1 month, replacement of the facility head, or closure of the facility: <Amended 2018.12.18>
1. The facility no longer meets establishment standards;
2. In the case of a facility established and operated by a social welfare corporation or nonprofit corporation, the corporation's establishment permit is revoked;
3. An unlawful act, such as accounting fraud or infringement of users' human rights, is confirmed;
4. Activities are conducted during a suspension period;
5. This Act or an order under this Act is violated.
(2) Standards for dispositions by type of violation under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Gender Equality and Family. <Amended 2025.10.1>

Article 36 (Hearings)
Before ordering facility improvements, suspension of activities, replacement of a facility head, or facility closure under Article 35(1), the Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Special Self-Governing Province Governor, or head of a Si, Gun, or Gu shall hold a hearing. <Amended 2018.12.18>

CHAPTER 9 SUPPLEMENTARY PROVISIONS

Article 37 (Prohibition on Disclosure of Secrets)
A person currently or formerly engaged in youth welfare work at the Youth Counseling Institute, a youth counseling and welfare center, or a support center for youth with a migrant background (hereinafter "youth welfare support institutions"), or at a youth welfare facility, shall not disclose secrets learned in the course of those duties.

Article 38 (Prohibition on Use of the Same Names)
No entity other than a youth welfare support institution or youth welfare facility under this Act may use the name Korea Youth Counseling and Welfare Institute, youth counseling and welfare center, support center for youth with a migrant background, youth shelter, youth self-reliance support center, or youth treatment and rehabilitation center.

Article 39 (Supervision)
(1) Where necessary, the State and local governments may order a youth welfare support institution or youth welfare facility to report or submit data concerning its work, accounting and property, or have public officials enter the premises to inspect books and other documents or question staff.
(2) Public officials entering premises and conducting inspections under paragraph (1) shall carry proof of their authority and present it to the persons concerned.

Article 40 (Budgetary Subsidies)
Within budgetary limits, the State and local governments may subsidize all or part of the budgets needed for operation of youth welfare support institutions, youth welfare facilities and relevant organizations.

Article 41 (Evaluation of Institutions and Facilities)
(1) The Minister of Gender Equality and Family and Mayors or Do Governors may periodically evaluate the work performance of youth welfare support institutions, youth welfare facilities, and institutions or organizations entrusted with youth welfare work under this Act, as prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Gender Equality and Family. This shall not apply if a performance or management evaluation has been conducted under other legislation. <Amended 2025.10.1>
(2) The Minister of Gender Equality and Family may take measures such as reflecting the results of evaluations under paragraph (1) in supervision of and support for youth welfare support institutions and facilities. <Amended 2025.10.1>

Article 42 (Delegation of Authority and Entrustment of Work)
(1) Part of the authority of the Minister of Gender Equality and Family or a Mayor or Do Governor under this Act may be delegated respectively to a Mayor or Do Governor or head of a Si, Gun, or Gu, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended 2025.10.1>
(2) Part of the work of the State or a local government under this Act may be entrusted to youth organizations as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 42-2 (Entrusted Operation of Youth Welfare Support Institutions)
(1) Where necessary, youth welfare support institutions or youth welfare facilities established by the State or a local government under this Act may be entrusted to youth organizations for operation.
(2) Matters necessary for the standards and methods of entrusted operation under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Gender Equality and Family. <Amended 2025.10.1>

CHAPTER 10 PENALTIES

Article 43 (Penalties)
(1) A person who, in violation of Article 12-2(9), uses data or information from the integrated information system for other purposes or provides or discloses them to a third party shall be punished by imprisonment for no more than 5 years or a fine of no more than 50 million won. <Added 2021.3.23>
(2) A person in either of the following categories shall be punished by imprisonment for no more than 2 years or a fine of no more than 20 million won: <Amended 2021.3.23>
1. A person disclosing health examination results in violation of Article 8;
2. A person disclosing secrets in violation of Article 37.
(3) A person in either of the following categories shall be punished by imprisonment for no more than 6 months or a fine of no more than 5 million won: <Amended 2021.3.23>
1. A person establishing and operating a youth welfare facility without filing the report under Article 32(2);
2. A person continuing activities or operating a facility despite an order suspending activities or closing the facility under Article 35(1).

Article 44 (Joint Penalty Provisions)
Where the representative of a corporation, or an agent, employee or other worker of a corporation or individual, commits a violation under Article 43 in connection with the business of that corporation or individual, the corporation or individual shall also be subject to the fine specified in the relevant Article, in addition to punishment of the offender. However, this shall not apply if the corporation or individual exercised due care and supervision over the relevant business to prevent the violation.

Article 45 (Administrative Fines)
(1) A person in either of the following categories shall be subject to an administrative fine of no more than 5 million won:
1. A person using the same name in violation of Article 38;
2. A person failing to report or submit data under Article 39(1), or refusing, obstructing or evading an inspection.
(2) A person failing to report suspension, closure or resumption of operation in violation of Article 33 shall be subject to an administrative fine of no more than 3 million won.
(3) A person in either of the following categories shall be subject to an administrative fine of no more than 500,000 won:
1. A person transferring or lending, or receiving a transfer or loan of, a youth card in violation of Article 4(2);
2. A person manufacturing or using a certificate with the same name or marking as a youth card in violation of Article 4(3).
(4) Administrative fines under paragraphs (1) through (3) shall be imposed and collected by the Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Special Self-Governing Province Governor, or head of a Si, Gun, or Gu as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended 2018.12.18>
